k1061306022.notes: Teal fascia over the fish-market stalls at Heraklion harbour, seen at an angle from a dash camera. Main line is lowercase cursive-style Greek with accents on ή and ά; the small capital subline is low resolution but readable. The museum banners (ΙΣΤΟΡΙΚΟ ΜΟΥΣΕΙΟ ΚΡΗΤΗΣ / HISTORICAL MUSEUM OF CRETE) and PARKING sign across the street are distractors.

A white van partly hides the shop front but not the lettering. Vertical PARKING sign at right is a distractor.

p0c9ed2a342.notes: Shop fascia in Psyrri, Athens. The top line 'METAL FOR FASHI...' is cut off by the frame and the right end of every line (the rest of the first Greek line, fax numbers, a second TEL number) is hidden behind a pole, so only the visible parts are transcribed; the ΤΣΑΝΤΩΝ line continues with a hidden word ending in ...ΩΝ. Graffiti overlaps the left of 'ΑΦΟΙ'. A small blue street plate at far right reads ΟΔΟΣ ΑΓΙΑΣ ΕΛΕΟΥΣΗΣ / AGIAS ELEOUSIS (partly hidden); alternative query 'Αγίας Ελεούσης'.

c73670545.notes: Corfu old town. Small shield-shaped hanging shop sign far down a narrow alley, in a decorative archaic Greek letterform (Σ drawn as a sideways M-like shape). A smaller line above, probably a proprietor name ending '...ΣΟΥΛΑΣ', is too small to read reliably and is left out. Graffiti on the left wall is a distractor.

c166455716.notes: Athens (Thiseio/Petralona area). Small blue street plate high on a wall, shot from below; Latin line faded. To its right an older painted name '...ΑΣΙΩΝ' on the wall is cut off. Graffiti ('SKA' etc.) and a meter box labelled '206' are distractors.

c24129263.notes: Chania, Crete. Frontal blue municipal street plate on a stone wall; white Greek, yellow Latin. House-number range panel underneath.
